title: Tags
html:
Tags in Baldur's Gate 3 are identifiers attached to creatures. They can have various effects on gameplay, like enabling additional dialogue options, or deciding whether the creature can be targeted by certain spells. There are many different tags throughout the game. Some are defined by a character's background and inherent traits, while others are obtained by performing certain actions.

Overview

Tags are attached to characters and serve a few different purposes. Most tags are used for dialogue options; for example, monk-specific dialogue options are enabled via the Monk tag. Tags like Branded are required to use certain features of items. Which tags apply to a character can be found at the bottom of the 'Detailed View' in the character panel. Note that not all tags that appear next to dialogue options are necessarily linked to a character tag; for instance, the Illithid option shows up in conversations but is not a tag in the character panel.

Below follows a list of all possible tags in the game:

Race

Each race grants its specific name as a tag.

  •  Human
  •  Elf
  •  Drow
  •  Half-Elf
  •  Half-Orc
  •  Halfling
  •  Dwarf
  •  Gnome
  •  Tiefling
  •  Githyanki
  •  Dragonborn

Subraces

Most subraces grant a tag as well. Notably, dragonborn subraces do not have any tags.

  •  High Elf

  •  Lolth-Sworn Drow

  •  Asmodeus Tiefling
  •  Mephistopheles Tiefling
  •  Zariel Tiefling

Class

Paladins do not have a class tag, only a tag for their chosen subclass. Clerics also lack a class tag, only having a special tag based on their chosen deity. Picking another class via multiclassing also grants that class's tag.

  •  Barbarian
  •  Bard
  •  Druid
  •  Fighter
  •  Monk
  •  Ranger
  •  Rogue
  •  Sorcerer
  •  Warlock
  •  Wizard

Subclass

Only paladins and warlocks have tags for each of their subclasses. For barbarians, only the Berserker subclass has a tag.

  •  Berserker
  •  Oath of Devotion
  •  Oath of the Ancients
  •  Oath of the Crown
  •  Oath of Vengeance
  •  Oathbreaker
  •  The Archfey
  •  The Fiend
  •  The Great Old One
  •  The Hexblade

Cleric deity

Clerics get their class tag named after their chosen deity. The  Cleric of Shar is a special tag exclusive to  Shadowheart for as long as she stays loyal to Shar during the game.[1] After a specific moment in Act Two, she can switch her tag to  Cleric of Selûne.

Additionally, characters multiclassed into both cleric and paladin receive another tag corresponding to their deity. The ability for paladins to choose a deity was removed after Early Access, but paladins with cleric levels may still receive these tags. Similar to the cleric tag, there exists a special  Paladin of Shar tag exclusive to  Shadowheart.

Origin characters

All origin characters and companions have a tag specific to them.

  •  Astarion
  •  Gale
  •  Lae'zel
  •  Halsin
  •  Jaheira
  •  Karlach
  •  Minsc
  •  Minthara
  •  Shadowheart
  •  Wyll
  •  The Dark Urge

Special tags

Outside of the tags mentioned above, additional tags exist which do not fall into any category.

  • Baldurian – granted if a character's race is not from the Underdark ( Deep Gnome,  Drow,  Drow Half-Elf,  Duergar) or Astral Plane ( Githyanki)
  • Branded – getting branded by  Gut or  Greez in the Shattered Sanctum
  • Dark Justiciar – given to  Shadowheart upon staying loyal to Shar and killing the  Nightsong
    • This can also be acquired by any character for attacking Nightsong from beyond normal Ranged Attack distance while she is still caged.
  • Detect Thoughts – while under the effects of the spell or having the means to cast it
  • Faithwarden – completing ⁠Investigate Kagha as a druid, if  Kagha survives
  • Forbidden Knowledge – upon partially deciphering the  Necromancy of Thay
  • Hag-Eyed – accepting ⁠Auntie Ethel's deal in Act One
  • Humanoid – always granted, but can be (temporarily) removed, see shapeshifting
  • One-Eyed – granted if:
    • Character is  Wyll (he has one stone eye made out of  Bloodstone[verify])
    • Character has  Volo's Eye after agreeing to Volo's surgery during Act One or Act Two
  • True Soul – granted after using  Illithid Persuasion seven times[verify]
  • Underdark – granted if a character's race is from the Underdark ( Deep Gnome,  Drow,  Drow Half-Elf,  Duergar)

Special interactions

Disguise self

While using  Disguise Self or similar effects, tags granted by race and subrace will be removed and replaced by the race of the chosen disguise. The subrace of the disguise is predetermined and cannot be changed. For instance,  Disguise Self: Masc Dwarf turns the player into a  Gold Dwarf, granting both the Dwarf and Gold Dwarf tags.

Similarly, disguise effects temporarily remove the Branded tag, causing effects which require the Brand of the Absolute to no longer work, such as the  Gloves of Power.

Shapeshifting

Using either  Wild Shape or  Displacer Beast Shape temporarily removes the Humanoid tag until returning to humanoid form.

Becoming  Full-illithid permanently removes the Humanoid tag.

Notes

  1. ↑ This used to be available to all characters during Early Access but was cut before the full release. Additional cleric deities used to be available as well, see cut content.
